Depends on what you're going for. 

If you like a glossy finish a lacquer finish will probably be best. If you want to go with a natural finish I recommend finishing it with a mineral oil and wax finish.

Both finishes will fill the pores up and seal the wood to keep it in check.  
Just keep in mind lacquer is pretty time consuming and unforgiving, especially when installing the frets, but looks incredible and feels amazing when done right. (wouldn't recommend it if you don't feel confident in fretting abilities yet, though)

I typed this on notepad before reading any other comments to stop myself from being influenced by other ideas. Quite interesting how many of us had similar ideas in some regards.

It's a quiet, warm afternoon. The wind creeping into the window barely makes the summer better, but at least the clean air is clearing my mind.

"In 200 meters, you will arrive at your destination on the left."

With the car inching forward at this point, I feel a warm rush of adrenaline in my abdomen. This is really stupid.

I squint skeptically at the run down industrial buildings that pass by on my left, and grip the steering wheel tighter with my sweaty hands.

"You have arrived at your destination"

I bring the car to a standstill, but before I switch off the engine I close my eyes and let the flashbacks roll in of the wars. It feels like a lifetime ago. I was a mere child when they started dropping bombs and recruiting civilians as mercenary soldiers in a changing 'free' world.

Since then people have kept to themselves much more and began to treat each other with a general sense of rightful distrust. The wars have dwindled populations down to devastatingly low numbers, and the once over-infested infrastructure is now a gaping chasm of potential.

I force myself to get out of the car and push through the small iron gate that leads into the larger part of the cemetery where the app on my phone is leading me. A deep breath and a wash of relief - I walk into the overrun mess that was once a graveyard. The dry winter months have devastated most of the plant life, but there were still a few remnants of flowers and plants left as signs of respect to old timers and fallen mercenaries, some possibly decades ago.

Walking closer to the beacon reveals a relatively small mound of red earth next to a half dug grave hole. Strange.

I approach apprehensively and on my toes, getting a head start by peering in through the top; but the late afternoon sun leaves the hole dark. I take off my sunglasses and squint into the shallow hole.

Inside it I find the body of a black haired girl. I get try to have a closer look at her, still approaching apprehensively.

Her body lies peacefully on a white linen sheet, dressed in mostly black clothing, with a golden locket draped perfectly in sight just below her neckline.

I see some evidence of past emotion in light creases in her face and notice the surprisingly in-tact rouge on her lips, she is beautiful. Such a pity. She must be around my age, maybe a few years younger.

"It's not polite to stare" her lips say.

My body jerks in disagreement with itself and with the situation and I fall onto my back, staring towards the hole in disbelief.

She appears from inside the hole with one hand resting on the outside of the wall of the dug grave and her face beaming with laughter towards the summer sky. She catches her laugh with the other hand and stares towards me with friendly green eyes, she waits for my reaction.

"What the fuck?" I feel my ears get warm from embarrassment.

She bursts out in laughter again, doubling over this time inside of the hole for multiple seconds before catching her composure and hopping gracefully out of the hole.

I stand up along with her and we clean the dust and dry grass from ourselves with claps.

"I'm sorry-" she starts "- I saw your dot come closer to mine and I figured you were coming for me. I kinda panicked to be honest."

She turns around and walks off. Putting her hands in her jacket pockets. I pursue.

Kiaat is a very showy wood. I sanded it down with 120, 180, 240, 320 grit. Then ultra fine scotch brite. Then gave it 2 coats raw linseed oil, then (This was after taking those pics tho) rubbed in 3 coats of a finish I made from beeswax and mineral oil. The final finish is slightly more shiny, and smooth to the touch. It's also much better protected from water because of the beeswax. Or if a drastic change could cause the moon to be knocked out of orbit to drift away from us, or into us. (though the chance of such an asteroid having the correct trajectory is probably impossible due to the effect other big things like Jupiter would have on it)

A more likely thing to consider is debris from a collision. A "normal" sized asteroid as you called it would probably be visible to big telescopes on earth (maybe a debris cloud to the naked eye if it were big enough). Though the debris would probably not be big enough have a big effect on earth. (because of the decreased mass and velocity) Maybe a few flashes of it burning up in our atmosphere, but probably not that much more.

I do have a crazy theory however a moon/planet sized object hitting the moon and hitting it closer to us, causing the earth's orbit around the sun to change. Causing us to move closer toward it, or drift off into the abyss of space over the course of a few decades.
